answer.location_description: Whole image: a periodic horizontal stripe (grating) pattern spanning all rows and columns. Rows come in alternating pairs with a 4-pixel period: rows 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, 12-13, 16-17 and 20-21 bright, and rows 2-3, 6-7, 10-11, 14-15, 18-19 and 22-23 dark.
answer.mechanism: Hidden units 1, 8, 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29 are stripe detectors. Their weights are positive on row pairs 0-1, 4-5, 8-9, … and negative on the alternate pairs, and their biases are strongly negative (-36 to -97), so they stay off on ordinary images and fire only when this grating is present. They feed layer-2 units u3, u4, u10, u12 and u13 positively (e.g., u4 gets 63, 63, 74, 83, 93, 59 from units 9, 10, 20, 24, 27, 29), and those units have positive output weights (+63, +77, +67, +42, +71). The same stripe units feed u1 and u7 negatively, and u1 and u7 have large negative output weights (-94, -99), so turning them off also pushes the logit up. A second group, units 2, 3, 23 and 31, carries the opposite phase with large positive biases (65-99). These units drive u1 and u7, so when they are active the output moves toward benign. A grating in the first phase therefore raises the malignant logit.
answer.evidence: The 4-row-period sign alternation is consistent across all of units 1, 8, 9, 10, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 29. Unit 8, for example, has rows 0-1 at about +25, rows 2-3 at about -30, rows 4-5 at about +35 and rows 6-7 at about -35, continuing through row 21. Units 2, 3, 23 and 31 show the exact phase-inverted pattern. A uniform-width, full-image periodic row structure is not a property of a nodule or of lung anatomy. These are among the largest-magnitude first-layer weights, and they route through the strongest layer-2 and output weights (u4: 77, u13: 71, u7: -99, u1: -94). The remaining units (0, 4-7, 11-17, 19, 21, 22, 25, 26, 28, 30) look like unstructured noise.
answer.main_feature: Beyond the stripes, the same units carry a localized blob near rows 10-15, cols 9-19 (e.g., strongly negative weights at r10-11, c16-19 in the stripe units and positive in the anti-phase units). This suggests a weak sensitivity to nodule density and texture near the centre, but most of the discriminative weight sits on the stripe grating.
